Per Court :-
1.

Heard the learned counsel for the applicant, the learned A.P.P. for respondent No.1 and the learned counsel for respondent No.2.
2.

The applicant seeks bail in C.R.No.67 of 2024 registered with Police Station Purna, Taluka Purna,
District Parbhani, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 304B, 306, 323, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
3. The applicant is the husband of the deceased.
The deceased committed suicide within four months of the marriage.
It was an allegation against the applicant that he was harassing her as her father did not pay him the balance dowry.
He also harassed her for bringing money from her parents to purchase a motorbike.
The parents had made the part payment to him.
The deceased was ill- treated physically and mentally.
The victim was complaining about her ill-treatment to her parents on the phone.
On the day of the incident, she called her parents and said that the applicant asked to make arrangements to pay the remaining dowry amount and money to purchase a motorbike.
She was ill-treated for the 3 939-BA-868-24.odt remaining amount of dowry and for the new motorbike.

She committed suicide on 19.03.2022.
4.
Learned counsel for the applicant argued that he was to attend the Zilla Parishad Office to report his joining as a Teacher on 24.05.2024.
Considering the situation, this Court was pleased to grant him temporary bail for the purpose of joining services.
Since the day of his release, he has been enjoying the bail granted to him for the purpose of attending the Zilla Parishad Office on 24.05.2024.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that the false allegations have been levelled against the applicant.
He never ill-treated the deceased for demanding a balanced dowry and motorbike.
He was a meritorious student in his education career.
Since the day of marriage, she has been quarrelling with the applicant and his family.
She had disclosed to him that she had an affair with someone.
Hence, she did not want to reside with him.
For these reasons, she committed suicide.
She died within a short period.
The applicant has been languishing in jail under the presumption of law.
The applicant has a good future.
The investigation has been completed.

sentences.text: He also argued that the further detention of the applicant would serve no purpose.
Therefore, the applicant may be granted bail.

6. Learned A.P.P. and the learned counsel for the victim/parents 4 939-BA-868-24.odt submit that the deceased had no reason to make a false allegation of demand of dowry and motorbike and harassment for these demands.
The deceased never disclosed her affair with another man.
The applicant also never complained to the parents that she had an affair with another man and that she did not want to cohabit with him.
The defence is an afterthought.
The applicant's educational merits are not concerned with the crime.
Within four months, a young lady has to finish her life.
Prima facie evidence is against the applicant that he was harassing her for demand of dowry and motorbike.
There is nothing with the applicant to rebut the presumption of commission of the offence.
The offence is serious.
Hence, the applicant may not be granted bail.
7. Perused the papers placed before the Court.
8. Admittedly, the incident happened within four months after marriage.
The first information report is that the victim was complaining against the applicant about the demand for a motorbike and the balance of the dowry.
The material further reveals that the amount in part was paid to the applicant.
He was also doubting the character/chastity of the deceased.

On the day of the incident,
the deceased made a phone call to her mother and told her that she should arrange for the remaining dowry amount and motorbike.
If that is not paid, they will not keep her alive.
These are the strong allegations against the applicant.
A legal presumption is running against the applicant.
He never complained about the victim's unwillingness to stay with him or any other relative.
Reading the papers as a whole, it appears that the prima facie case is against the applicant.
The offence is serious.
A young lady has lost her life for not fulfilling the demand of the applicant.
10. For the above reasons, the Court is not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
Hence, the application stands dismissed.
11. Criminal Application No.2368 of 2024 for the production of documents stands allowed.
12. Criminal Application No.2444 of 2024 stands disposed of.
13. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant wanted to approach the Honourable Supreme Court, interim bail granted under order dated be extended for two weeks.
14. The applicant has joined as a Teacher as per the interim bail granted to him.
However, the learned A.P.P. for the State and learned counsel for the victim opposing the application would submit that considering the offence's gravity, interim bail should not be extended.
